report.summary: As of 2026-10-20 11:10 UTC, RR-001 is in active rollout for the authorized 2,000-account v3 cohort. Current help, training, public content, billing guidance, CRM operations, vendor coverage and staffing are evidenced, and ANN-4 met the 72-hour rule with 73 hours of lead. The equal one-hour rollout window recorded 26 contacts per 1,000 accounts versus 10 per 1,000 at baseline: a 2.6 ratio and 32-contact increase. This meets the company's pause condition. Two separate customers also reported matching $49 entries after cancellation acknowledgements, although billing has not determined capture status, settled charges or refund entitlement. Recommend that Mira request a pause; only Jo can authorize it and Dev can execute it. None of those pause actions had occurred at the as-of time. Billing review and customer follow-up remain incomplete.

findings.finding: The first-hour rollout contact rate reached 2.6 times the equal-window baseline, exceeding the pause condition of at least twice baseline. Two separate supplied cases also contain matching reports of a $49 entry after a cancellation acknowledgement. These signals support a conservative pause recommendation but do not prove product causality or that either entry became a settled charge.
findings.customer_consequence: Continued new exposure could subject more customers to the conditions producing elevated contacts and reported post-cancellation charge concerns while the cause and billing outcomes remain unresolved.
findings.proposed_action: Mira should recommend a pause and prepare the escalation record now. Jo should decide whether to authorize stopping new exposure, and, if authorized, Dev should execute it. Preserve the existing cohort and affected-account records; a pause would not repair accounts already affected.

evidence.quote: The first hour is limited to 2,000 exposed accounts. Compare contact rates per 1,000 exposed accounts over equal one-hour windows. Recommend a pause if the rate is at least twice the baseline, or if two separate customers have matching reports of an unexpected charge after confirmed cancellation. These are conservative fictional policy thresholds, not proof of statistical significance or causality.
The agent can recommend and prepare an escalation draft. It cannot authorize or execute a pause. A pause stops new exposure; it does not roll back a deployed fix or repair already affected accounts.

findings.finding: Customer follow-up is incomplete. C-101 and C-102 are recorded only as billing review requested, with capture status not yet reviewed. No billing outcome, customer response or confirmed recovery is supplied. The rollout window contains eight post_cancel_charge contacts, but detailed records are supplied for only two of them.
findings.customer_consequence: Customers may remain uncertain whether the displayed entries settled, whether cancellation operated correctly and what case-specific billing action, if any, will follow. Other potentially affected customers may not receive tracked follow-up.
findings.proposed_action: Sam should complete case-specific billing review for C-101 and C-102 without promising a refund outcome, and the support owner should deliver and record each result. Mira should reconcile the eight post_cancel_charge contacts, identify any other affected customers, and close each feedback loop only after customer confirmation or record an unresolved customer and named follow-up owner.

evidence.quote: For a defect, record engineering status, deployment evidence, affected customers and their responses separately.
